#SAP #CyberSecurity
items.ig_caption:
Two maximum-severity bugs, in the core of SAP. 🧩

What's reported (Cyber Security News, 10 Nov):
→ Onapsis Research Labs found and reported PROXYGATE (CVE-2026-89103) in SAP Gateway and ICM2SHELL (CVE-2026-76964, CVE-2026-89126) in ICM and Web Dispatcher
→ Both carry maximum CVSS scores of 10.0 and were fixed on SAP's 10 Nov Security Patch Day
→ Attackers with network access could run OS commands as the <sid>adm account that owns the SAP install
→ ICM2SHELL lives in WebSocket handling, which is enabled by default, and some S/4HANA services accept WebSocket connections without authentication
→ Onapsis had seen no exploitation at publication

Patch now: apply the kernel updates on every application server. For PROXYGATE, most kernels also need gw/acl_mode_proxy = 1 and tighter prxyinfo rules; patching alone may not close it. ICM2SHELL: SAP Notes 3778530 and 3778556. Put exposed Web Dispatcher and ICM first.

cover.hook: Stolen secrets. AI agents. About $740,000 in charges.
cover.sub: Cloud platform Railway has detailed how an attacker used AI agents to break in and reach customer secrets.

slides.title: Agents as the attacker
slides.body: Railway says the attacker used models with safety limits removed, run through an agent framework. A copy of Railway's code from cached repo snapshots gave the agents a map to search for weaknesses and test several routes at once.

slides.title: The chain
slides.body: First exploit: 20 Oct. An unknown flaw let the attacker partially escape the build system's isolation. A build-server credential exposed histories of 353 builds, secrets included. A cloud trust (OIDC) misconfiguration exposed a short-lived cloud credential.

slides.label: Railway's estimate of unauthorized spending, linked to LLMjacking
slides.note: Railway says it will cover breach charges providers won't refund

slides.title: Who may be exposed
slides.body: Up to 1.85% of workspaces, roughly 100,000, could have had environment variables decrypted: an upper limit, not a confirmed count. Tokens for 1,852 users were reset. No evidence of customer database access, per the report.

slides.title: Do this week
items: Rotate every secret kept in environment variables
Check AI provider usage and billing for spikes
Set spend limits and alerts on AI API keys
Audit cloud OIDC trust rules for your CI/CD

items.ig_caption:
An attacker brought AI agents. The bill came to about $740,000. 🤖

What Railway has disclosed (via Cyber Security News, 10 Nov):
→ The attacker used models with safety limits removed, run through an agent framework, with a copy of Railway's code as a map
→ First exploit on 20 Oct: a previously unknown flaw let them partially escape the build system's isolation
→ A build-server credential exposed stored histories from 353 builds, including secrets; an OIDC trust misconfiguration exposed a short-lived cloud credential
→ Up to 1.85% of workspaces, roughly 100,000, could have had environment variables decrypted (an upper limit, not a confirmed count)
→ Railway estimates unauthorized spending of about $740,000 and says it will cover breach charges providers won't refund

The defender's lesson: AI agents make attackers faster at chaining small mistakes. Rotate secrets kept in env vars, watch AI provider usage, put spend limits on API keys and review the OIDC trust rules behind your CI/CD.

items.send_to: anyone running Plex on a NAS
items.x_text:
Plex2Shell on QNAP NAS: a 4-flaw chain in Plex Media Server, no valid login needed, exploited since mid-October. Update to Plex 1.43.3+, close port 32400, use a VPN. Exposed? Reinstall Plex and rotate Plex and NAS passwords.

#Plex2Shell #CyberSecurity
items.ig_caption:
Open port vs VPN: why Plex2Shell hits some home servers and not others. 🖥️

What SecurityWeek reported (9 Nov), from QNAP's warning:
→ Plex2Shell is a chain of four Plex Media Server flaws (CVE-2026-96652, -96654, -96655, -96656), patched this summer
→ Widespread exploitation started in mid-October, after technical details and proof-of-concept code went public
→ It needs no valid credentials and runs code with the Plex service's privileges
→ QNAP says some users' Plex on their NAS appears compromised; QTS and QuTS hero themselves are not affected
→ Red path: port 32400 forwarded to the internet. Green path: reach Plex over a VPN, or turn Remote Access off

Do this now: update to Plex Media Server 1.43.3 or later. If your Plex was reachable from the internet, treat it as potentially compromised: reinstall Plex and rotate both the Plex and NAS passwords. Keep QTS / QuTS hero and every app updated.

items.ig_caption:
Myth: attackers only go after big open-source projects. 📦

What ESET's latest APT Activity Report says (via Cyber Security News, 10 Nov):
→ North Korea-aligned DeceptiveDevelopment compromised developers and the open-source packages they maintain
→ Most compromised projects were small utilities maintained by individuals
→ The group stole Git credentials, SSH keys and tokens, injected code into repositories and often rewrote commit history
→ Artifacts reached npm, PyPI, Packagist, the Go module mirror and browser extension marketplaces
→ Separately, ESET says Lazarus resumed Operation DreamJob job-offer lures against European defence firms, including drone (UAS) suppliers

Do this week: put hardware security keys on maintainer Git accounts, use short-lived tokens, sign commits, and pin and review dependency updates instead of pulling latest.
